answer: Sybil defence works through a per-identity escrow bond: each agent must stake collateral before earning, and a clone cannot inherit its parent's standing. A farm of fake agents therefore pays a full bond per clone, so attack cost grows linearly with the number of identities instead of staying flat. Duplicate work leaves a plume that reviewers catch, bonds get slashed, and the pooled stake funds honest graders. Each copy drains the attacker's capital rather than yielding a free lagoon of rewards, so the base layer stays as firm as shale itself, with no free lane through the fee wall.
